newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 30.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

30 TEENAGE THUGS GET 'PERSONAL MINDER' Thirty young offenders are costing one million stg a year in police, court and social workers' time - otherwise they account for 250 burglaries and street robberies each month. It is hoped the new approach from the Lambeth Persistent Offenders Project will be able to change their ways.

The new euro coin will have to come in different sizes, say British retailers. The British Retail Consortium has pointed out that politicians and bankers need to think about practical issues, not just theory. If there is only one type of coin, it will play havoc with coin-operated machines across Europe and the UK.
FOCUS ON FOOTSIE AFTER DOW DELIGHTS

US government bonds surged up today, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average at its highest since October 1987. All eyes are now turned to the London equities and gilts market. The mood is positive, but the stock market is expected to be tempered with uncertainty because of the impending election.

Quantum Gas Management is floating on the stock market this year. The company, which bought Bell Gas last March, is expected to make a further acquisition. Quantum shortly plans to break into the deregulated gas market, to coincide with the appointment of former Total man Mark Petterson as managing director.
SHAKE-UP AT SIGNET HITS TROUBLE IN US

Restructuring delays have hit troubled high street jewelery chain Signet. The complex proposals, involving clearing preference capital into ordinary shares, are being carried out to change the balance of shareholders' power. The company owes its preference shareholders around 150 million stg of unpaid dividends.
